prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study was a prospective single-center cohort involving 33 adults scheduled for CAR T-cell therapy, using a digital platform with 25 cognitive, visual, and graphomotor tasks plus a symptom questionnaire at baseline.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: For follow-up assessments after infusion and before discharge, researchers chose about eight tasks for each participant rather than repeating the full set.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: All 33 enrolled patients finished the baseline assessment, and 30 of them completed both follow-up assessments.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Two patients died before follow-up could occur, and one patient stopped the planned treatment due to clinical instability and did not undergo follow-up.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Only 4 to 11 patients had paired baseline and pre-discharge data for each specific task, and the changes in task scores and reported symptoms varied widely.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In the three patients with documented grade 1 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, one reported higher fatigue and neuropathic pain, while another reported more dizziness and difficulty concentrating.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients who did not have immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome also showed nonspecific worsening of symptoms.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that nonrandom task selection, limited paired data, unvalidated task indices, and nonspecific symptom changes prevent conclusions about detecting neurotoxicity or the clinical utility of the tool.
facts.subject: humans
